claim: arch_diff_command.md contradicts itself about what happens to a malformed task journal. Its Responsibilities section (line 7) requires DiffCommand to "run the lifecycle pre-flight ([[a9aa93774cc2|ProjectResolver]]) to obtain the project context ... refusing an uninitialised or broken project with the pre-flight's own error and exit code instead of guessing." Its own removal-check paragraph (line 26) then says of the SAME task journal, now read at its resolved location: "A malformed journal degrades this to unverifiable notes rather than failing the run — a deliberately gentler contract than the retired bead-map's hard error on a corrupt file." Both sentences describe the one file at ctx.JournalPath.
authoritative_source: spec/lifecycle/arch_project_resolver.md's Responsibilities section and spec/lifecycle/test_resolver.md's "Broken is doctor's error" case are unambiguous: "`.spex/` present but the snapshot or journal missing or unparseable — broken; the error names `spex doctor`", and test_resolver.md spells out the journal case explicitly ("Repeat with the journal truncated to malformed bytes: same class of error"). ProjectResolver is this bead's own contract and is not in dispute; arch_diff_command.md's line 26 is the stale half.
evidence: This PR fixes cmd/spex/diff.go to thread the pre-flight's ctx.JournalPath into validator.CheckRemovedNames instead of dropping it (the read/review's blocker), so the removal sweep's journal source and the pre-flight's own journal check are now, correctly, the same file. Because runDiffE calls lifecycle.Resolve unconditionally before CheckRemovedNames ever runs, a malformed journal at .spex/history.jsonl is now caught by the pre-flight's checkJournalReadable (lifecycle/project_resolver.go) and returns a *BrokenError — exit 3, naming `spex doctor` — before the removal sweep's own gentle degradation (loadJournalNames returning nil on a parse error) is ever reached. `spex diff` can therefore never observe arch_diff_command.md line 26's "degrades this to unverifiable notes" outcome for a malformed journal; that sentence is now describing a CLI-unreachable code path. cmd/spex/diff_test.go's TestFR8_DiffCommand_MalformedJournalDegradesGently now asserts the exit-3/`spex doctor` outcome instead (the pre-flight's own, already-tested contract), matching what the shipped binary does. validator.CheckRemovedNames's own gentle degradation of a malformed journalPath argument still holds and is still exercised directly by validator.TestREQ_6f8284df92a2_MalformedJournalStillNotes, which calls the function without going through the pre-flight — so the library-level behaviour line 26 originally documented is not wrong, only unreachable through the one caller (`spex diff`) the leaf is describing.
proposed_fix: Reword arch_diff_command.md's line 26 to state that a malformed journal is caught by the lifecycle pre-flight before the removal sweep ever runs (refused as a broken project, exit code shared with the uninitialised case, naming `spex doctor` — per arch_project_resolver.md), and reserve the "degrades to unverifiable notes" language for the journal's genuine soft-failure mode: absence, which the pre-flight tolerates by resolving `.spex/` successfully and handing CheckRemovedNames a path to a file that simply is not there yet on a freshly-initialised project (spex init creates an empty journal, so this is really "no removed events recorded yet", not "no journal file"). Cross-reference test_resolver.md's already-covered malformed-journal-is-broken case instead of restating a contract the resolver already owns.
